articleTitle: Distributed intelligent actuators and sensors
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Distributed intelligent actuators and sensors (DIASs) are discussed. The DIAS project is the first stage towards realization of integrated automation within a control, maintenance and technical management system (CMMS). The concept of control islands, maintenance islands, and technical management islands is discussed. DIAS subsystems, methodology and demonstration sites are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Priority polling and dynamic time-window mechanisms in a multicycle Fieldbus
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Real-time local area networks have to handle synchronous and asynchronous data transfer. The data transfer is handled in two different phases or time windows. Priority polling algorithms that generate the polling sequence for the data transfer automatically respecting the periodic deadlines are presented. Dynamic mechanisms to extend time-windows are introduced and the network bandwidth is utilized more efficiently. These algorithms are computed during the real-time operation of the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some complexity metrics for object-oriented programs based on information flow
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A set of complexity metrics for object-oriented systems based on information flow models is presented. These metrics may be used to measure methods, classes, class hierarchies, and programs in an object-oriented system. The attributes to be measured are the interactive couplings among entities and the internal complexity of each individual entity. The proposed set of metrics is examined using Weyuker's meta-metrics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: APRIS: Automatic Pattern Recognition and Inspection System
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A fast visual automatic pattern recognition and inspection system is described. The major aim of the system is the recognition and inspection of 2D patterns and images in the printing industries. The strategy behind the system uses a hybrid structure combining the conventional n-tuple method and the pixel-by-pixel comparison method. Both of these methods lend themselves to a massively parallel hardware implementation using application specific integrated circuits (ASICs). High-density field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) were chosen for the implementation of the system, providing the high speeds required by the automatic recognition and inspection of modern automated assembly lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model for schema evolution in temporal relational databases
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: In temporal databases, transaction time and valid time are added to the data. In this context, the modification of the schema which a database management system (DBMS) can undergo during its lifetime, known as schema changes, must develop into the higher concept of scheme evolution. Changes to the schema produce versions of previous schemas along both time axes and these versions must be maintained and managed during the whole database life. An overview on the issues of temporal relational databases and relational schema changes is presented. A basic outline for the integration of these two aspects into a temporal relational database model supporting schema evolution is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation modelling for accumulation conveyors in transient behaviour
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The optimization of accumulation system monitoring requires the modelling and simulation of the system's transient behavior. Existing simulators are not accurate enough and are slow. The simulation model presented models the physical system very easily, without making rough estimates, by means of basis parameters (types and features of the batches and conveyors). It calculates the states of the system only when the system undergoes discontinuity (incoming and outgoing batches, shift in speed or behavior of a conveyor, etc.). This formalization is integrated in a model based on batch Petri nets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture of an MMS event manager
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Event management is often considered as the most complex functional unit of the Manufacturing Message Specification (MMS). A model for an MMS event manager, i.e., the entity within the virtual manufacturing device (VMD) that is responsible for the management of MMS events, is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new decentralized approach for FMS control
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: An approach for integrated flexible manufacturing system (FMS) control is developed. Decentralized control is examined and shown to compare favorably with conventional centralized control. It complies with the requirements of flexibility, reactivity, and accessibility for use on FMSs. The principles of a coordination founded on an event-based approach are given. A presentation model and its implementation principles are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Schedulability analysis of real-time systems using timing constraint Petri nets
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Timing constraint Petri nets (TCPNs) to facilitate the modeling and analysis of real-time systems are presented. The schedulability analysis capabilities of TCPNs are discussed. Through modeling, analysis, and iterative refinement, the software developer can verify whether an underlying specification will be schedulable with respect to the given timing requirements, all via the token game played in TCPNs. The schedulability of real-time systems against the imposed timing constraints is analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sequential fault diagnosis in system maintenance
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The results of the study of the impact of symptomatic information on sequential fault diagnosis are presented. Typical test sequencing algorithms based on the concepts from information theory and heuristic AND/OR graph search methods are considered. The estimation of optimal weights of statistical data of faulty elements associated with given symptoms is discussed. Empirical results are presented for the case in which the symptomatic information is processed separately and in advance of the global failure rate data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: UTARK: an object-based real-time kernel for distributed embedded systems
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: UTARK (University of Texas at Arlington Real-time Kernel) is a real-time kernel designed to cope with the complexity of software for real-time embedded systems. The concepts behind the design of UTARK are described. Three major issues, i.e., communication, scheduling, and fault tolerance support, are discussed, along with a new development model for large, complex, distributed embedded real-time systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance engineering throughout the product life cycle
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A methodology for integrating performance engineering into the software development cycle is described. This approach is being tested by a number of products as part of the development of new performance engineering procedures. Early results show a dramatic performance improvements when performance engineering is started early in the product lifetime.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated visual inspection of galvanized and painted metallic strips
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A vision system designed for automatic inspection of galvanized and painted metallic strips is described. After a description of the image acquisition device, the different original algorithms which detect and recognize flaws on the strips are presented. These tasks are run in real-time on a specific hardware structure. The prototype described is integrated on a production line to evaluate its efficacy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Method for a design of distributed control systems
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A method for the design of modular programs for distributable applications in the process control domain is presented. By 'distributable' is meant applications which can be distributed on a network after their specification and programming. In addition to the advantage of delaying the binding time, this method also allows safe design. It relies on the formalism of interpreted Petri nets (IPNs). All transformation primitives that contribute to the method produce IPNs with good qualities. It is based on a priori safe design, not on a posteriori verification, and on three key points: a global methodology which describes the steps to be followed and their ordering; a common description formalism which is used for all the steps (specification, organization, validation, and evaluation); and three complementary design techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electronic data interchange (EDI)-definition-justification-implementation
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A general discussion of electronic data interchange (EDI) is presented. EDI is defined, and its domain is indicated. Economic issues specific to EDI are discussed. An approach for project management and implementation is suggested. The possible future effects of EDI on business are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Users' requirements specification for control: an object-oriented approach
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The users' requirements specifications is used for the development of control systems. After considerations about the qualities that such a specification must have, the principles of a method to guide the requirements expression are presented. The approach is organized in a hierarchy which is based on levels of abstraction. Each entity is modeled by an object which is specified and then decomposed in accordance with principles which are oriented to the expression of needs. Principles are defined to favor the external specification of behavioral requirements which are formalized with statecharts. An example of the application of the approach is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specification and validation of time constraints with the HMS machines model
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The validation and method integration process at different stages of the life cycle of an industrial production system are discussed. Method evaluation is emphasized as a preliminary step in project development. An approach for method scope assessment is proposed. The approach is based upon a model for describing the method's structure and artifact transformation. This model, when used for a particular method, viz. the hierarchical multi-state (HMS) method, allows the determination of aspects not clearly defined by the method as well as the identification of the boundaries of the method. It is then possible to propose an integration scheme where the aspects not taken into account by the method are covered by complementary methods. As a validation, an example of the use of HMS in compliance with the proposed integration is presented. The time constraint validation possibilities of HMS are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling and design of a production automated system using a decisional object oriented method 'MACSOOD'
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Because of the lack of design methods and graphic software in the field of production automatized systems (PASs), a design support system which guides in the analysis and PAS design has been developed. This tool, called MACSOOD, is based on a decisional object-oriented method because, at the technical level, the assumptions of an object oriented design and of an object programming are the best known answers to the problem of re-use and flexibility. The design process is discussed, from the construction of hierarchical trees of objects to the verification of coherence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthetic intelligence-application to the automatic design of automobile transmission
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: An implementation of an automatic design method, the constructive-deductive (CD) method, is presented. Emphasis is placed on the application of synthetic intelligence in the automatic design of new power transmissions. A detailed example of the design of an automotive transmission is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Significant states and decision making for real time workshop scheduling
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: To execute a production plan in the disturbed environment of a manufacturing workshop, real-time scheduling methods and tools are needed. The associated real-time decision making problems are described. Significant resource and operation states for decision making are identified. This induces the set of significant events which must be detected by means of the shop-floor real-time monitoring system. The relationships between states and events are described using Petri nets. The two main types of decisions for real-time scheduling are briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A trajectory generation module for 2D and 2D1/2 environment
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A trajectory generation module for a mobile robot in a 2D environment and for a robot arm in a 2D1/2 environment made of low height objects placed on a work surface is discussed. For the mobile robot, the problem of driving into a narrow corridor is solved by means of a backtracking process. Obstacle avoidance is carried out by taking into account only the wrist and the end effector of the robot. This allows the determination of a grasping configuration of convex and concave objects, and allows the choice of the shortest, collision-free trajectory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robot programming system for research purposes
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The hardware and software structure of the ASEA IRp-6 robot control system is presented. It has been developed to make both the hardware and software architecture open for research and teaching purposes. The user can communicate with the robot controller through a direct access interface between the host computer and the controller itself. The main part of the software is a library of subroutines of a modular and open architecture. Several experiments are carried out on the system and show that it can be programmed in a flexible way.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integration of communication system by the information system study
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The information system usually implies the use of the entity-relationship formalism at conception level and database for the implementation aspect. But the information is not only located in the database but also in the communication system. During the information system design, the conceptual stage is not changed. At the logical step which describes the data organization, both database and communication aspects are taken into account. The logical analysis must generate the database structures and the manufacturing message specifications (MMS) configuration of all equipment which corresponds to the physical stage. Some concrete rules which permit translation of the entity relationship formalism to MMS objects and MERISE communication model to organize each VMD are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System for defect detection on material
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A hardware and software solution allowing, in a given experimental environment, defect detection during textile manufacture is defined. The method is based on detecting breaks in the periodicity of the fabric's pattern. If the periodic characteristic of the material is deleted by filtering, the defect is detected more easily.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assembly oriented production planning
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A new architecture for a production planning system (PPS) is presented that is aimed at factories containing flexible assembly cells with significant setup times. The system uses dynamic programming to determine an optimal assembly schedule. The planned assembly order start dates resulting from this schedule are used by a standard materials requirement planning (MRP) system, to generate orders for parts and subassemblies. This is different from a normal situation, where due dates in the master production schedule are used by the MRP system. A better match between the assembly schedules and the arrivals of parts and subassemblies can be achieved in this way, which results in a reduction of inventory levels and lead times.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach for process control
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: An original approach to a control process based on a distributed blackboard system is presented. This blackboard architecture, formed of blackboard systems, can be viewed as a multiagent system. Two concepts mark the authors' approach to process control: the human presence and real time. A study is proposed of the blackboards for process control and a methodology adequacy to build blackboard based software for robotic control is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trajectories optimization by environment acquisition for autonomous mobile robots
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The importance of environment acquisition in free-path finding trajectories in mobile robotics is discussed. A technique is proposed to allow the operator to perform environment acquisition by means of HAMID (heuristics for autonomous mobiles with integrated design). Both the breadth-first search (BS) and the depth-first search (DS) are applied to this representation for free-path finding trajectories. Clothoid insertion to smooth the chosen trajectories is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integration of heterogeneous software packages in the field of production management and production control systems: a view of generic problems and a conceptual approach
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Existing supervision software packages are frequently designed without the possibility of integrating them with any other computer applications. The integration is one of the important keys for the implementation of the CIM concept. An analysis of the existing supervision software packages is presented and compared with industrial needs. Based on that analysis, a new architecture for the supervision integrated systems is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated control units for production machine
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A description model is presented, and it is shown how it permits better definition of the organization of the algorithms of a control unit for a production machine. This unit is capable of driving coordinated axis movements with a certain degree of autonomy and to a near-optimal standard. On the basis of this model, a partly decentralized control unit (ARIEL) is designed and realized. It includes a power converter unit and sensor system. The final goal is to associate these control units and their actuators, which are thus transformed into a simple computer peripheral unit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effective implementation of SPC in wide area manufacturing systems (A case study)
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Statistical process control (SPC) is a tool for monitoring the manufacturing process. To be effective, SPC must be coupled with a system for solving problems. The use of computer systems and a special organizational structure to achieve an effective SPC implementation are discussed. The facility is considered to be a wide area manufacturing system (WAMS) because various manufacturing support groups are located in different buildings around the manufacturing facility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Documentation system study for automated production system maintenance
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The maintenance of a complex APS (automated production system) is very difficult. The re-use of the documents produced throughout the APS concept within a software engineering environment framework is proposed. It requires the elaboration of a technical document model. A data reference model (standardized in France: Base-PTA NF Z68901) relative to an APS is used. The DAE (documentation atomic element) concept is proposed for the link between a documentation base and an application base.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The 'OLYMPIOS' model: an algebraic specification for modelling the information system of a manufacturing enterprise
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A means of specifying industrial information which is used in a model of an information system for manufacturing enterprises called OLYMPIOS is presented. This specification is based on abstract data types and algebras, and simplifies the industrial information by separating it into three terms: data, time, and organization. Such an algebraic specification is used to design a representation of the information system of manufacturing enterprises. It is included in computer aided software engineering (CASE) tools for computer-aided consulting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CALS: An essential strategy for paperless interchange of technical information for manufacturing-current and future standards
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Computer-aided acquisition and logistics support (CALS) is a Department of Defense and industry initiative, consisting of strategies, technologies, concepts and standards to reduce time-to-market, reduce costs and improve the quality of multiple-contractor projects (initially weapons systems). The evolution of CALS is summarized from paper flow to integrated and digital technical information, shared by government and contractors. Current and future CALS standards are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Object-oriented flexible and integrated manufacturing system modelling
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The authors describe the concept of an object oriented manufacturing modeling methodology characterized by its flexibility, which can support the multiple stages of the manufacturing system planning procedures, and by its potential to combine conventional CAE software modules. Rapid designing, from the rough design process to the development of control logic in manufacturing systems, can be achieved with this approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discrete events system modelling and software engineering: ACSY
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The increasing complexity of manufacturing systems requires performing methods, models, and tools for the design of control software. The system command analysis (ACSY) model is a CASE (computed aided software engineering) type model based upon the cooperation of models belonging to the set of disparate models: flow diagrams, standard IEC 848 Function Chart for Control System (FCCS), and a data processing language and data structure called Dictionary. The Software Producer, which is developed in object-oriented design is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A case-oriented expert system for materials handling
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: In automatic assembly, the feeding of different components of a product is often performed by automatic vibratory and centrifugal feeders. Their design remains largely empirical, especially for their associated orienting systems (OSs). A case-oriented approach for computer-aided design of the OS is proposed. The objective of the proposed approach is not only to realize the computer-aided design of the OS, but also to attempt to introduce the CBR (case-based reasoning) approach in the ESs (expert systems) in this field. In order to apply CBR, the orienting process is modeled. A prototype is tested and validated for possible future industrial applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RDA integration in an open system architecture for CIM
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The goal of the CIMOSA project is to provide an open system reference architecture which covers all the information needs in a manufacturing enterprise. Among all the forthcoming open systems interconnection (OSI) standards, CIMOSA has chosen the RDA (remote database access) protocol as the access protocol for the information services. The motivation of this choice, the common concepts and an example of mapping between the information services and RDA services are discussed. The deficiencies of the RDA standard as compared to the CIMOSA requirements are indicated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design by interpolation
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The design of shapes by interpolation, that is, cases where the desired shape is somehow 'in between' two given shapes, is discussed. The main issues involved in design by interpolation are: (a) capturing the 'nature' (behavior) of the guiding shapes A and B; (b) attaining automatic correspondence between points (i.e., which point in shape A should be associated with which point in shape B); and (c) determining the interpolation method. New techniques for capturing the 'nature' of shapes and for determining automatic correspondence of points are presented. Examples for interpolation of polygons, curves, and surfaces are included. The possibility of future design based upon extrapolation, rather than interpolation is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The Fieldbus, a worldwide challenge FIP, second generation technology
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The Fieldbus is intended to connect in an open way a number of field devices of various origins, providing industrial control and various other functionalities at low cost. Several approaches have been set: minimalist, specialist, and global. In the standardization domain, various organizations act in this field. IEC, ISA, CENELEC, DKE, and UTE are the international bodies concerned with this activity. The first generation of FIP components from CEGELEC is available on the market, including FULLFIP, FIPLD1 and FIPTR1. The second generation provides industrial and highly competitive FIP components in addition to meeting IEC physical layer compatibility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An advanced planning and control system for discrete manufacturing
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The main results achieved in the ESPRIT project IMPACS (Integrated Manufacturing Planning And Control System) are presented. IMPACS covers the complete hierarchy of production planning and control. It requires integrated solutions and decision making. The premise of IMPACS is that no amount of sophisticated tools and techniques to automate and computerize production planning and control are really useful unless they are developed within an architecture context. This architecture is associated with a methodology which shows how to use the architecture to implement the IMPACS in a particular enterprise, taking into account its specific requirements. A computer tool set called CAGIM (Computer Aided General IMPACS method) is developed to support the use of the architecture and methodology. An overview of the IMPACS project, IMPACS architecture and methodology, as well as the CAGIM tool is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of a methodology and computer based teaching tool for the cost justification of world class manufacturing techniques, tools and technologies
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A new approach to the cost justification of world class manufacturing tools, techniques, and technologies, entitled PROFIT (program for financing integrated technologies), through the use of a structured approach, ensures that the full costs and benefits, both tangible and intangible, of one or more proposals are considered, and that the important company wide aspects are not overlooked. The approach is easy to use and understand, thereby making the best use of valuable management time, and, by being based on sound accounting principles, is acceptable to a company's bankers and accountants.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implantation oriented methodology in design control of flexible manufacturing systems
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A computer-aided design methodology for flexible manufacturing system control with a view to industrial implementation is presented. In the modeling phase, based on the Petri net formalism, generic aspects which allow the use of an object-oriented approach are discussed. The CASPAIM II (Conception Assistee de Systemes de Production Automatises en Industrie Manufacturiere) project methodology employs a product approach and integrates the planning, the scheduling, and the treatment of failures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient encoder for distributed real-time applications
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Standard basic encoding rules are too elaborate and inefficient for distributed real-time applications. Two major obstacles encountered are long protocol data units and slow encoding times. The problem of encoding for real-time applications is addressed. Taking Fieldbus as a representative of real-time networks, it is shown why the encoder should be simplified and how this can be done. The impact of encoders, in general, on the overall network performance is studied. Implementation results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed encoder.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A conceptual data scheme for integrated maintenance: A map to design maintainable AMS
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The maintenance of large automated manufacturing systems (AMSs) requires the integration of various maintenance tools. Results of a research project concerning data exchanges between design tools and maintenance tools (GAMA project: Genie Automatique pour la Maintenance) are presented. A complete prenormative conceptual data schema for integrated maintenance of AMSs is developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A help for solving dilemmas encountered in flow analysis
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The workshop layout in production cells by material flow analysis implies the solving of several problems. These are expressed in terms of production management aims and they are related to the CIM concept. A consensual research method which uses cross-classification techniques is suggested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Object data base. AI and CAD-CAM: application to the process ascending generation (PAG) concept
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: An approach called process ascending generation (PAG) to generate sequences of operations for a given machining feature is presented. The PAG determines the sequences of operations for a given feature, starting from its finished state and, by successive steps, leading up to its raw state. The object modeling problem is solved for some machining features and for an object database called Cutting Tool Chart (CTC). The CTC is a new concept used to model the abilities of the cutting tools to perform a machining feature. A forward-chaining rule-based strategy is used to implement the PAG concept in Prolog language. All of those aspects are implemented on CAD-CAM software, which is constituted by an object oriented database (OODB) and an integrated AI language.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A generic activity manager for a control engineering workbench
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The design of a control engineering framework should rely on software engineering framework architecture models. The ECMA model divides integration framework services into four management subsystems in order to efficiently support development processes; user interface, tool, object, and activity managers. The design of an activity manager is discussed. It is generic, and once configured by a process model, it controls the progress of a project so that it follows the rules defined in this model. The way to integrate this activity manager into a framework is described. The expected benefits for project management of such architectural solutions are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementing a business data warehouse approach in a semi-conductor manufacturing plant
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The business data warehouse approach at the IBM Corbeil-Essonnes plant is described. Both concept and implementation aspects are discussed. The author focuses on the end-users computing services (EUCS) point of view including the satisfaction of user needs as well as the organizational and technical approach of this nonapplication environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Visual perception in industrial automation
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: An overview of computer aided vision is presented. Specific topics addressed include functional analysis of the vision process; the difficulties and current limits of computer aided vision, including noninvariance of data in rotation and translation, and problems of perspective; the industrial applications of artificial vision; management of an artificial vision project; and the French market for artificial vision.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Structured documentation systems for aircraft engine manufacturing
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The implementation of technical documentation systems in SNECMA production facilities is described. The needs are explained. The functionalities are detailed, together with the structure of the documents. A solution is given in terms of hardware and software, with examples from operational systems. The benefits of such projects are indicated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time and industrial local area networks
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Time aspects of industrial local area networks are analyzed. Research on and the verification of an architecture satisfying time constraints are discussed. The concept of communication transactions associated with different cooperation models is introduced. These are client/server, client/multiserver, multiclient/multiserver, and producer/distributor/consumer. The architecture of time-critical communication systems is analyzed, with emphasis on the necessity of explicit time management by services and protocols under the control of the end user.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synchronous programming: introduction and application to industrial process control
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Synchronous languages and their potential applications to industrial process control are discussed. The synchronous approach to real time system programming is described. Ongoing research on synchronous programming in industrial process control applications is reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expression and verification of temporal constraints for real-time systems
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A preliminary approach to deal with timing constraints is given. It is shown how to analyze the notion of temporal constraints, and a simple way to express them using the notion of language is proposed. To test the temporal aspects of a full verification, an execution trace on the acceptor of the language is checked. This allows testing of a full specification expressed in any formalism.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated data management in a heterogeneous CIM environment
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The state of the art in CIM is characterized by islands of automation. In order to bridge the gaps between such islands of automation, appropriate frameworks must be developed for the integration of heterogeneous CIM application systems. One aspect of such frameworks, i.e., data integration is discussed. Different alternative approaches to data integration are presented, and their relative merits and shortcomings are discussed. The approach developed within the SUKTIS project which is dedicated to the integration of heterogeneous application systems within the area of mechanical engineering is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data access protocols for integrated engineering environments
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Open access to distributed information stores is a problem in integrated engineering environments. Data access protocols provide a common interface for the access to information stores. Several file transfer and database access protocols are standardized in the context of the ISO open system interconnection reference model. The Document Filing and Retrieval Protocol Standard (DFR) is compared with alternative solutions such as FTAM (File Transfer Access and Management) or RDA (Remote Database Access). Evaluation criteria are introduced, and the suitability of the protocols for the use within integrated engineering environments is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TRACK II: A multi-processor robot controller
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Advanced robotic systems require a multiprocessor architecture, a real-time operating system and appropriate interfaces. The asynchronous nature of these systems causes non-deterministic behavior and poor reliability. The specification and design of a high-performance controller for advanced manipulation systems is presented. The controller has a modular parallel architecture which can be extended without performance degradation, a synchronous real-time operating system and a kit of hardware modules. The authors' design philosophy aims for maximum real-time computing power by exploiting the computational characteristics of robot control and planning algorithms, together with minimum software development effort, at the expense of CPU utilization.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A CNC model well-suited for the requirements of CNC software construction environment
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Any environment allowing operator-assisted design and construction of computerized numerical controller (CNC) software should rely upon an underlying generic CNC architecture meeting certain requirements, such as: support for a high degree of reusability; real-time system support; an associated method; and a hierarchical approach. The requirements of such an environment for a generic CNC architecture or model are specified. Most existing architectures are considered and are shown to be incapable of satisfying these requirements properly. A new model meeting the needs of the environment is then proposed, and the real-time part of this model, the executive, is described in detail. Elements of an associated method that provides the human operator with a sequence of steps guiding the specification of requirements of a specific CNC to be built in the model of the environment are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Database model for design data
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A construction database model (CDM) used for the conceptual level modeling of design objects is presented. A primary purpose of the CDM model is the modeling of hierarchically structured objects and construction dependencies among objects. CDM is an attribute-based data model. The CDM model represents various abstractions identified in certain semantic database models by means of attributes. To distinguish between different abstractions, the notion of attribute role is introduced. Special attention is paid to the representation of derived properties of the object. They are described by means of a constructor. The constructor makes possible the description and reevaluation of the design object construction process. The CDM is used as a data model for a storage system designed for storing data in CAD applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture of the control system of a mobile robot based on the use of a real-time multitasking executive with an expert system
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A hierarchical control system of an autonomous mobile robot which has to travel in a quasi-static environment is studied and implemented. The architecture of the control system involves three levels: planner, navigator, and pilot. From a cartography of the environment, the planner elaborates all the possible paths to reach a goal from a starting point. The algorithm used is based on the traversability concept. The planner level does not operate in real time. With the information given by the planner, the navigator defines a constrained optimal trajectory. The navigator is able to avoid an unexpected obstacle on the defined trajectory and the navigator works under real-time constraints and a multitasking mode. The pilot manages the sensors (odometry, telemetry) and the feedback control of the robot actuators. These tasks are decoupled from those executed by the main processor. The three hierarchical levels are designed with a real-time multitasking operating system associated with an expert system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: After CAD: Automatic design: dream or reality?
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: In mechanical design, current CAD systems can only perform two kinds of tasks: calculation of the performance of already designed elements, and final drafting of assembly and detail drawings prior to manufacturing and filing. The creative tasks remain the exclusive domain of man. A new concept, called synthetic intelligence, seems to be able to do creative tasks. An example is given. The first commercially available truly generative process planner (KRONOS) does perform such work. KRONOS, composed of a part editor, a technological preprocessor, a logic module, and a technological module, is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Feature recognition from 2D and 3D modellers
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: It is established that feature recognition is the area which needs concentration for a totally automated process planning system (APPS) and the cornerstone for developing downstream application programs to a higher degree. In that context, important feature aspects and the philosophy behind feature based systems are presented. Well-known works and recognition techniques developed in the three-dimensional domain are surveyed. The 2-D context is also examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Outline for discrete part manufacturing engineering
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: It is argued that within the framework of computer integrated manufacturing and engineering reference modeling, manufacturing system models may be and must be verified by prototyping supported by computer-aided methodology rather than by paper-aided methodology. Both synchronic and diachronic life-cycles as employed in integration engineering are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method for assembly system design including an integrated computerized design support
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: When using computerized design support, structuring of both the design process and the parameters influencing the design is necessary. In order to facilitate a systematic design process, an approach to a system design method (SDM) is developed. This method consists of thirteen phases. A computerized design support system is integrated into the method, helping the system designer develop and evaluate assembly system alternatives. The structuring of the information concerning the assembly system design is carried out through a classification of the parameters, and by system parameter analysis. The relationship between the system design method, the computerized design support and the system parameters is important.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Realisation with constraint programming of leveled and sequenced schedule for discontinuous process systems
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Studies on models and tools for production control of discontinuous process systems have been made by the laboratory 'Genie Industriel et Logiciel' of the University of Valenciennes and the 'Institute Productique' of the Sligos Company. They have led to the development of a model of leveled scheduling and of sequenced scheduling for batch production systems. Experiments on the prototype model indicate its validity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Command recording versus parametric and variational systems, an old/new third way of parametrizing CAD models by end users
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The two major ways of parametrizing in CAD are analyzed, and new results obtained with command recording are presented. The major improvement is a purely interactive definition of classic control structures in structured programming, which allows end-users to make powerful programs (parameterized pieces) with minimal programming knowledge. Despite commercial trends, neither of the methods may be considered to be universal. Depending on the precise goals of the user (prototyping, simple and well-defined components modeling, or complex components modeling) the features required for parametrization systems may vary according to the different qualities of either system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Factory-level supervision based on real-time cellular object architectures
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: An architecture for the supervisory control of flexible production processes at the factory level is introduced. The architecture is based on the idea of concurrent synchronous cellular logic and its extensions in the form of multi-level hierarchical structures. Active cellular objects are used to provide real-time behavioral templates which can be instantiated at any time by translating the formal process specifications given in the form of a colored Petri net. The resulting architecture exhibits high-performance characteristics through its parallel organization and very high flexibility through its modular template-like structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Definition of a methodology for mechanical conceptual design
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: The design process and the modelling possibility in the conceptual design stage are discussed. Two different approaches are proposed in mechanical design: axiomatic and AI. The axiomatic approach is used to seek basic principles (or laws) for decision making in each stage of the design, while the AI technique allows modelling of the intuitive knowledge and experiences which expert designers use in a well-defined domain. In order to truly help designers, the most effective strategy for elaborating powerful computer-aided design system is to combine these two types of approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simulation system for coordinated manipulation
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: A special-purpose simulation system for constraint-based manipulation with robotic devices is described. This system is a computational tool for the study of task-directed programming of robotics. The architecture of the system is outlined, the module for controlling independent fingers cooperating for the task of part rotation is described in detail, and experiments are reported. This implementation contributes to a deeper understanding of the properties of algorithms for fine motion planning for dexterous manipulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proceedings of COMPEURO '93
publicationTitle: 1993 CompEuro Proceedings Computers in Design, Manufacturing, and Production
abstract: Presents the front cover of the proceedings record.
